title: Got to celebrate the opening of @Joe Turner’s Come and Gone & Taraji’...
transcript: There's nothing like a Broadway opening night, and I got to celebrate the opening of Joe Turner's Come and gone with seven Daughters Wine. Taraji P. Henson is one of my favorite actresses, and getting to see her make her Broadway debut was so special. And seven daughters is her wine, and they actually sell it at the theatre, so obviously it is a perfect combination. Joe Turner's Come and gone is part of August Wilson's Pittsburgh Cycle, which is a series of plays that each document a different decade of black life in America. Joe Turner takes place in 1910 in a boarding house in Pittsburgh. Taraji plays Bertha Holly, who runs the boarding house alongside her husband Seth, played by Cedric the entertainer. I thought the entire cast was incredible, and the story was so compelling. It's a powerful story about identity and freedom and what it means to truly find yourself again after everything has been taken from you. It's such a layered show and feels so relevant even 40 years later. From there, we headed over to the after party to celebrate with everybody. Seven daughters kept the wine flowing and the vibes good all night long. We had both the seven daughters Moscato and the seven daughters Sweet Red Blend, and I even got to meet Taraji P. Henson herself self and congratulate her on her opening night. It was so cool. I will literally never forget it. So thank you, seven daughters, for inviting Me to be a part of this unreal evening. And make sure you go and see Joe Turner come and gone on Broadway. And when you're there, head to the bar and try out Taraji's wine.
